hints: Apply Newton's second law to the trailer of mass $350\text{ kg}$: $T - 120 = 350(0.4)$ to find the tow-bar tension $T$.
Apply Newton's second law to the whole system of mass $4850\text{ kg}$: $2500 - (X + 120) = 4850(0.4)$.
Solve both linear equations to determine $T$ and $X$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Equation of motion for the trailer alone.
The trailer has mass $m_T = 350\text{ kg}$ and acceleration $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$. The horizontal forward force is the tension $T$ from the tow-bar, and the backward resistance is $120\text{ N}$:
$$T - 120 = m_T a$$
$$T - 120 = 350 \times 0.4$$
$$T - 120 = 140$$
$$T = 140 + 120 = 260\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Equation of motion for the combined system.
The total mass is $M = 4500 + 350 = 4850\text{ kg}$. Internal tension forces cancel out, leaving the driving force $2500\text{ N}$ forward and total resistance $(X + 120)\text{ N}$ backward:
$$2500 - (X + 120) = M a$$
$$2380 - X = 4850 \times 0.4$$
$$2380 - X = 1940$$
$$X = 2380 - 1940 = 440\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Verification on the van alone:
$$2500 - T - X = m_V a$$
$$2500 - 260 - 440 = 1800$$
$$4500 \times 0.4 = 1800\text{ N}$$ (Consistent).
